newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam seeks to punish major foreign investor.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam seeks to punish major foreign investor.

text.p: Vietnam on Wednesday announced fines and punitive steps against Peregine Capital Vietnam, marking the latest twist in a lengthy investigation into alleged business irregularities by a major foreign investor.

The Communist Party's Nhan Dan newspaper carried details of a decision by the Ho Chi Minh City authorities of a proposed fine of $50,000 for Peregrine and a range of penalties against associated firms.
A People's Committee official in the southern city said at least 13 companies were involved, and all were being punished for alleged violations of Vietnamese laws on foreign businesses.
The measures included fines of between $900 and $9,000 and the withdrawal of licences from eight firms connected with Peregrine's chief executive in Vietnam, Nguyen Trung Truc.

Company officials refused comment, but a source close to Truc, an Australian-Vietnamese businessman, and the Hong Kong-based firm painted a different picture of events and said the matter was far from being concluded.

"These fines are proposed fines for administrative violations only, and they have to be discussed with the local authorities first. We want to get on with business and we're seeking advice on how to sort this out."

Alan Mercer, chief legal counsel with Peregrine Investments Holdings Ltd in Hong Kong, said: "Needless to say we are reviewing the situation in Vietnam with a view to discussing with the authorities the amount of the fine."
He said the fine related to Peregrine's operation from an unregistered office without a licence in Vietnam.
He said he had no further comment but the company planned to issue a statement.
Peregrine's high-profile run-in with the authorities began last May when state investigators turned up unannounced at the company's office in Ho Chi Minh City.
Company officials said it was a "routine" check, but within weeks a separate probe was launched into the tax affairs of Truc and his wife, and they were barred from leaving Ho Chi Minh City.

The source said the authorities in Ho Chi Minh City (formerly Saigon) continued to hold their passports pending the outcome of the case. He also said Australian diplomats were continuing their efforts to resolve the matter.
